summary: Reproduced the reported crop on the authenticated web receiver while a Pixel 7 Android 17 device was sharing its screen. The browser displayed a 576×1280 stream in a landscape stage but clipped the portrait frame. The video was already configured with object-fit: contain; the grid item retained its automatic intrinsic minimum size and was cut by the stage's overflow:hidden. Setting min-width and min-height to zero lets the player shrink to the stage and contain the full frame.

checks.name: Live browser receiver reproduction
checks.observation: The web client showed the Pixel 7 publication Pistol121_android at 576×1280 and 1.5 FPS. A browser screenshot visibly showed only the upper part of the portrait phone UI filling the landscape stage. The browser and Android client were both connected to SHARE_TEST with microphones disabled.

checks.name: Screen-share lifecycle cleanup
checks.observation: Tapped the Pixel app's accessibility-labelled Stop screen sharing control. Android dumpsys media_projection then reported Media Projection: null; the browser receiver reported the selected stream ended.

checks.name: Portrait player layout regression test
checks.command: cd frontend && npm run test -- src/voice/screen_viewer_reference.spec.ts
checks.observation: The new regression assertion failed before the CSS fix because the screen player lacked min-width: 0 and min-height: 0; after the fix all 10 focused tests passed.

checks.name: Frontend production build
checks.observation: vue-tsc and Vite production build passed. Vite emitted its existing informational large-chunk warning for the LiveKit bundle.

checks.name: Production stylesheet deployment check
checks.command: Fetch https://v.bootybay.ru/ and its linked CSS; inspect the .screen-player rule
checks.observation: On 2026-09-30, the production page and linked stylesheet returned HTTP 200, but .screen-player contained object-fit:contain and max-height:100% without min-width:0 or min-height:0. This confirms the local crop fix is not deployed. No production state was changed.

remaining: Deploy the frontend change, then repeat Pixel portrait screen sharing in a browser and confirm all four source edges after attach, resize/rotation and fullscreen. Also compare the Android stream in the Flutter receiver; sender/receiver dimensions alone do not prove full-frame rendering. The 2026-09-30 production CSS check confirms the deployed bundle still lacks min-width:0 and min-height:0; deployment requires authorization.
